title: Stair Stringer Calculator
cardBlurb: Risers, treads, stringer length, and an IRC check
seoTitle: Stair Stringer Calculator - Rise and Run
metaDescription: Find the number of steps, exact riser height, total run, stringer length, and angle for a total rise in inches, checked against 2021 and 2024 IRC stair limits.
secondaryKeywords: how to calculate stair stringer length
intent: Find the number of steps, exact riser and tread sizes, stringer length, and angle for a given total rise, and check them against IRC limits.
registerRow: Keyword Register: stair stringer calculator (Volume 1, Competition ease 4, Ad value 2, Fit 4, Priority 8); launch order 6
intro: Enter the total rise from finished surface to finished surface to get the number of risers, the exact riser height, the stringer length, and a check against the IRC's riser, tread, and 3/8 in limits.
diagramCaption: Stringer profile of your stair (longest flight). It redraws as you type.
uniqueAddition: Code check against both the 2021 IRC (R311.7.5.1, R311.7.5.2) and 2024 IRC (R318.7.5.1, R318.7.5.2) section numbers, with a local-amendment override for the maximum riser and a 3/8 in uniformity check on the 1/16 in layout, plus a stringer length table for 2 to 12 risers.

inputs.name: totalRise
inputs.label: Total rise
inputs.help: Finished surface at the bottom to finished surface at the top (deck boards or floor), 6 to 200 in.

inputs.name: tread
inputs.label: Tread depth (run per step)
inputs.help: Horizontal run of each step, nosing to nosing, 8 to 14 in. The IRC minimum is 10 in.

inputs.name: maxRiser
inputs.label: Maximum riser height
inputs.help: The IRC maximum is 7 3/4 in. Change it only if your local code amends it (some allow 8 1/4 in).

inputs.name: landing
inputs.label: Landing partway up
inputs.help: Splits the risers as evenly as possible between two flights. The landing replaces one tread.

inputs.name: nosing
inputs.label: Nosing
inputs.help: How far each tread board overhangs the riser below, 0 to 1.5 in. It sets the tread board depth, not the run.

outputs.name: uniformityCheck
outputs.label: Risers within 3/8 in when marked to 1/16 in

sources.title: 2021 International Residential Code Visual Interpretation (Stairway Manufacturers' Association, hosted by Viewrail): R311.7.5.1 risers 7 3/4 in maximum, R311.7.5.2 treads 10 in minimum, 3/8 in variation
R318.7.5.1 Risers, 2024 IRC (Stairway Manufacturers' Association blog)
R318.7.5.2 Treads, 2024 IRC (Stairway Manufacturers' Association blog)
2024 International Residential Code, Chapter 3 Building Planning: Section R318.7.5 Stair treads and risers (International Code Council)
